claim: Patched1 (Ptch1) contains two 'PPXY' motifs that serve as endocytic sorting signals directing it to degradation in lysosomes.
source: Here, we report endocytic sorting signals for the receptor Patched1 (Ptch1), comprising two 'PPXY' motifs, that direct it to degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, and it is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1-3 demonstrating the role of PPXY motifs in Ptch1 localization and stability.

claim: The PPXY motifs of Ptch1 are recognized by HECT-domain ubiquitin E3 ligases Smurf1 and Smurf2.
source: These signals are recognized by two HECT-domain ubiquitin E3 ligases, Smurf1 and Smurf2, which are induced by Shh and become enriched in Caveolin-1 lipid rafts in association with Ptch1.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 7F, FRET analysis in Figure 7C-E, and co-sedimentation experiments in Figure 1E.

claim: Smurf1 and Smurf2 are induced by Shh.
source: These signals are recognized by two HECT-domain ubiquitin E3 ligases, Smurf1 and Smurf2, which are induced by Shh and become enriched in Caveolin-1 lipid rafts in association with Ptch1.
evidence: The abstract states this, and Figure 5E,G shows RT-PCR and RT-qPCR data demonstrating Shh induction of Smurf expression.

claim: Smurf1 and Smurf2 become enriched in Caveolin-1 lipid rafts in association with Ptch1.
source: These signals are recognized by two HECT-domain ubiquitin E3 ligases, Smurf1 and Smurf2, which are induced by Shh and become enriched in Caveolin-1 lipid rafts in association with Ptch1.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by confocal imaging in Figure 7A showing colocalization of Smurf2CG and Ptch1-RFP in Cav-1 positive lipid rafts, and co-sedimentation data in Figure 1E.

claim: Smurf-mediated endocytic turnover of Ptch1 is essential for its clearance from the primary cilium.
source: Smurf-mediated endocytic turnover of Ptch1 is essential for its clearance from the primary cilium and pathway activation.
evidence: The abstract states this, supported by data in Figure 3A,B showing accumulation of PPXY motif mutants in primary cilia, and Figure 5C,D showing Ptch1-GFP accumulation in cilia after Smurf knockdown.

claim: Smurf-mediated endocytic turnover of Ptch1 is essential for Shh pathway activation.
source: Smurf-mediated endocytic turnover of Ptch1 is essential for its clearance from the primary cilium and pathway activation.
evidence: The abstract states this, supported by luciferase reporter assays in Figure 4A showing that Δ2PY mutant fails to confer Shh inducibility, and Figure 5F,H showing loss of Gli1 induction in Smurf-deficient cells.

claim: Removal of both Smurf1 and Smurf2 completely abolishes the ability of Shh to sustain the proliferation of postnatal granule cell precursors in the cerebellum.
source: Removal of both Smurfs completely abolishes the ability of Shh to sustain the proliferation of postnatal granule cell precursors in the cerebellum.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data in Figure 10 showing reduced NeuN-positive granule cells in cerebellar slices after Ad-cre infection, and blocked GCP proliferation after Smurf knockdown.

claim: Shh specifies spatial tissue patterns during development by providing positional cues embedded in its concentration gradient.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Jiang and Hui, 2008; Robbins et al., 2012; Ryan and Chiang, 2012).

claim: Neighboring progenitor cells in a developing field can discern incremental changes in the Shh signal strength and adopt their respective fate accordingly during embryogenesis.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Ribes and Briscoe, 2009; Balaskas et al., 2012).

claim: Shh plays a crucial role in guiding the differentiation of tissue-specific stem cells in the adult.

claim: Colocalization between Ptch1-GFP and endogenous Lamp1 was revealed with the use of leupeptin.
source: We could not detect vesicles marked positively with both Ptch1-GFP and Lamp1-RFP or Ptch1-GFP and endogenous Lamp1-RFP without blocking lysosomal enzymes by leupeptin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), but colozalization between Ptch1-GFP and endogenous Lamp1 was revealed with the use of leupeptin (Figure 2C).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 2C and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Ptch1-GFP did not colocalize with either transfected Rab5-RFP or endogenous Rab5 without or with ShhN treatment.
source: We did not see Ptch1-GFP colocalizing with either transfected Rab5-RFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) or endogenous Rab5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) without or with ShhN treatment.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Endocytic cargos of caveolae are unloaded directly to late endosomes, bypassing early endosomes.
source: These observations are consistent with the notion that endocytic cargos of caveolae are unloaded directly to late endosomes, bypassing early endosomes (Quirin et al., 2008; Hayer et al., 2010; Sandvig et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Quirin et al., 2008; Hayer et al., 2010; Sandvig et al., 2011) and is consistent with the data showing Ptch1 colocalizing with Rab7 but not Rab5.

claim: Δ2PY-GFP was never found together with any of the three endosome/lysosome markers (Rab7, Lamp1, Rab5).
source: In contrast to Ptch1-GFP, Δ2PY-GFP was never found together with any of the three endosome/lysosome markers and ShhN treatment caused no statistically significant change thereof (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), indicating that Shh is not able to induce Δ2PY to move beyond lipid rafts to enter late endosomes.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 2A–C and Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2 and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Shh is not able to induce Δ2PY to move beyond lipid rafts to enter late endosomes.
source: In contrast to Ptch1-GFP, Δ2PY-GFP was never found together with any of the three endosome/lysosome markers and ShhN treatment caused no statistically significant change thereof (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), indicating that Shh is not able to induce Δ2PY to move beyond lipid rafts to enter late endosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing lack of colocalization of Δ2PY with endosome/lysosome markers (Figure 2A–C).

claim: Ptch1-GFP can proceed to late endosomes/lysosomes under the influence of ShhN in Kif3a−/− MEFs that do not make cilia.
source: Although Kif3a−/− MEFs do not make cilia (Chen et al., 2011), Ptch1-GFP could still proceed to late endosomes/lysosomes under the influence of ShhN unabatedly (Figure 2D,E), implying that Ptch1 endocytosis is downstream from or independent of ciliary trafficking.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 2D,E and represents data from confocal imaging experiments in Kif3a−/− MEFs.

claim: Ptch1 endocytosis is downstream from or independent of ciliary trafficking.
source: Although Kif3a−/− MEFs do not make cilia (Chen et al., 2011), Ptch1-GFP could still proceed to late endosomes/lysosomes under the influence of ShhN unabatedly (Figure 2D,E), implying that Ptch1 endocytosis is downstream from or independent of ciliary trafficking.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing Ptch1 endocytosis occurs normally in Kif3a−/− MEFs that lack cilia (Figure 2D,E).

claim: When re-expressed in Ptch1−/− MEFs, the 'PPXY' motif mutants accumulated in the primary cilium, in contrast to their wildtype counterpart.
source: However, we observed that when re-expressed in Ptch1−/− MEFs, the 'PPXY' motif mutants accumulated in the primary cilium, in contrast to their wildtype counterpart; ShhN treatment effectively forced Ptch1-GFP to exit the primary cilium, but it was less effective against these mutants (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3A,B and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: ShhN treatment effectively forced Ptch1-GFP to exit the primary cilium, but it was less effective against 'PPXY' motif mutants.
source: However, we observed that when re-expressed in Ptch1−/− MEFs, the 'PPXY' motif mutants accumulated in the primary cilium, in contrast to their wildtype counterpart; ShhN treatment effectively forced Ptch1-GFP to exit the primary cilium, but it was less effective against these mutants (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3A,B and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Ciliary accumulation of the 'PPXY' motif mutants is likely a consequence of their inability to endocytose, rather than a specific defect of ciliary export.
source: Ciliary accumulation of the 'PPXY' motif mutants is likely a consequence of their inability to endocytose, rather than a specific defect of ciliary export, since these mutants also accumulate in lipid rafts (Figure 1A,B) and blocking endocytosis with high concentration of leupeptin showed a similar effect without or with ShhN treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing mutants accumulate in lipid rafts (Figure 1A,B) and that blocking endocytosis with leupeptin shows similar effects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: The two 'PPXY' motifs play an equivalent role in regulating Ptch1 function in cilia.
source: Combined with results from the stability experiment (Figure 1F), this observation indicated that these two 'PPXY' motifs play an equivalent role in regulating Ptch1 function in cilia.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data from stability experiments (Figure 1F) and ciliary localization experiments (Figure 3A,B).

claim: Smo translocation into the primary cilium is an obligatory early event of Shh signaling and is concurrent to the exit of Ptch1 from the cilium.
source: To support this notion, we made temporal measurements of endogenous Smo translocating into the primary cilium, which is an obligatory early event of Shh signaling and was reported as concurrent to the exit of Ptch1 therefrom (Rohatgi et al., 2007a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature (Rohatgi et al., 2007a).

claim: In Ptch1−/− MEFs, Smo is constitutively present in the primary cilium.
source: In Ptch1−/− MEFs, immunofluorescence staining showed that Smo was constitutively present in the primary cilium (Figure 3C), as expected (Corbit et al., 2005; Rohatgi et al., 2007a; Kovacs et al., 2008).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C and is consistent with previous reports cited (Corbit et al., 2005; Rohatgi et al., 2007a; Kovacs et al., 2008).

claim: Re-introducing Ptch1-GFP cleared Smo out of the primary cilium in Ptch1−/− MEFs.
source: Re-introducing Ptch1-GFP cleared Smo out of the primary cilium, but ShhN treatment allowed Smo to move back in to nearly its full extent within 4 hr (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C,D and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: ShhN treatment allowed Smo to move back into the primary cilium to nearly its full extent within 4 hr after re-introducing Ptch1-GFP in Ptch1−/− MEFs.
source: Re-introducing Ptch1-GFP cleared Smo out of the primary cilium, but ShhN treatment allowed Smo to move back in to nearly its full extent within 4 hr (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C,D and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: ShhN treatment triggered the ciliary export of Ptch1 at a rate comparable to that of Smo import.
source: Conversely, ShhN treatment triggered the ciliary export of Ptch1 at a rate comparable to that of Smo import (Figure 3C, and compare Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C,D,E and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Re-introducing Δ2PY only allowed a substantially lower level of Smo to be imported back into cilia after ShhN treatment.
source: Re-introducing Δ2PY, on the other hand, only allowed a substantially lower level of Smo to be imported back into cilia after ShhN treatment and Δ2PY was itself resistant to Shh-induced export (Figure 3C,E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C,E and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Δ2PY was resistant to Shh-induced export from the primary cilium.
source: Re-introducing Δ2PY, on the other hand, only allowed a substantially lower level of Smo to be imported back into cilia after ShhN treatment and Δ2PY was itself resistant to Shh-induced export (Figure 3C,E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 3C,E and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Drosophila Ptc functions are twofold: first acting through Smo to negatively regulate downstream pathway signaling cell autonomously, and second, through ligand sequestration Ptc suppresses Hh signaling in neighboring cells.
source: As a ligand-binding and inhibitory receptor, the functions of Drosophila Ptc are twofold; first acting through Smo, Ptc negatively regulates downstream pathway signaling cell autonomously, and second, through ligand sequestration Ptc suppresses Hh signaling in neighboring cells.
evidence: This statement represents established knowledge about Drosophila Ptc function.

claim: When co-transfected with Ptch1-GFP, the 8xGliBS-luc reporter showed a robust inductive response to ShhN in Ptch1−/− MEFs.
source: When co-transfected with Ptch1-GFP, the 8xGliBS-luc reporter showed a robust inductive response to ShhN, resulting in a dose–response curve typical of a substrate-enzyme relationship; however, this reporter was barely induced by ShhN when it was co-transfected with Δ2PY (Figure 4A).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4A and represents data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The 8xGliBS-luc reporter was barely induced by ShhN when co-transfected with Δ2PY in Ptch1−/− MEFs.
source: When co-transfected with Ptch1-GFP, the 8xGliBS-luc reporter showed a robust inductive response to ShhN, resulting in a dose–response curve typical of a substrate-enzyme relationship; however, this reporter was barely induced by ShhN when it was co-transfected with Δ2PY (Figure 4A).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4A and represents data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The Shh signaling blockade imposed by Δ2PY could be by-passed by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Sufu.
source: The Shh signaling blockade imposed by Δ2PY could be by-passed by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Sufu (Figure 4B), a downstream negative regulator, suggesting that the blockade is pathway-specific and occurs upstream of Sufu function.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4B and represents data from luciferase reporter assays with Sufu knockdown.

claim: The blockade of Shh signaling by Δ2PY is pathway-specific and occurs upstream of Sufu function.
source: The Shh signaling blockade imposed by Δ2PY could be by-passed by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Sufu (Figure 4B), a downstream negative regulator, suggesting that the blockade is pathway-specific and occurs upstream of Sufu function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing that Sufu knockdown rescues the Δ2PY blockade (Figure 4B).

claim: In Ptch1−/− MEFs, 'PPXY' motif mutants were equally effective as wildtype Ptch1 or cyclopamine in suppressing 8xGliBS-luc reporter independent of the Shh ligand.
source: Indeed, in Ptch1−/− MEFs, these mutants were equally effective as wildtype Ptch1 or cyclopamine in suppressing 8xGliBS-luc reporter independent of the Shh ligand (Figure 4C).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4C and represents data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Δ2PY showed a robust inhibition of ligand-induced reporter activity in neighboring cells in the presence of limiting amount of ShhN (1:64 dilution).
source: In the presence of limiting amount of ShhN (1:64 dilution of the conditioned medium), Δ2PY showed a robust inhibition of the ligand-induced reporter activity in the neighboring cells; however this effect was nullified at high ShhN concentration (1:16 dilution) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4D and represents data from a mixing experiment with NIH3T3:GliBS-luc reporter cells.

claim: The inhibitory effect of Δ2PY on ligand-induced reporter activity in neighboring cells was nullified at high ShhN concentration (1:16 dilution).
source: In the presence of limiting amount of ShhN (1:64 dilution of the conditioned medium), Δ2PY showed a robust inhibition of the ligand-induced reporter activity in the neighboring cells; however this effect was nullified at high ShhN concentration (1:16 dilution) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 4D and represents data from a mixing experiment.

claim: Ptch1 engagement to the ligand can be regarded as an interaction that allows Shh to induce Ptch1 clearance from the primary cilium, the site of Shh signaling.
source: In summary, our data indicate that whereas Ptch1 engagement to the ligand may have a nominal effect of internalizing Shh, it can be also regarded as an interaction that allows Shh to induce Ptch1 clearance from the primary cilium, the site of Shh signaling, and this regulation equally impinges on both cell and non-cell autonomous signaling functions of Ptch1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data from Figures 3 and 4 showing Shh-induced Ptch1 exit from cilia and effects on signaling.

claim: Shh-induced Ptch1 clearance from the primary cilium equally impinges on both cell and non-cell autonomous signaling functions of Ptch1.
source: In summary, our data indicate that whereas Ptch1 engagement to the ligand may have a nominal effect of internalizing Shh, it can be also regarded as an interaction that allows Shh to induce Ptch1 clearance from the primary cilium, the site of Shh signaling, and this regulation equally impinges on both cell and non-cell autonomous signaling functions of Ptch1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data from Figure 4 showing effects on both cell autonomous (Figure 4A-C) and non-cell autonomous (Figure 4D) signaling.

claim: The C-terminal domain of Drosophila Ptc was shown to be recognized by Nedd4 HECT-domain E3 ligase.
source: Previously, the C-terminal domain of Drosophila Ptc was shown to be recognized by Nedd4 HECT-domain E3 ligase (Lu et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature (Lu et al., 2006).

claim: Mouse Nedd4 and Nedd4l did not promote Ptch1 degradation when expressed together with Ptch1-FLAG in HEK293 cells.
source: We expressed mouse Nedd4 and Nedd4l together with Ptch1-FLAG in HEK293 cells, and found that neither one promoted Ptch1 degradation, and several other HECT-domain E3 ligases including Wwp1, Wwp2, Huwe1, Herc1, Herc3, Herc4, Herc6, Hecw1, and Hecw2 also showed no effect, but co-expression of Smurf1 or Smurf2 did (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5A,B and represents data from Western blot analysis.

claim: Several HECT-domain E3 ligases including Wwp1, Wwp2, Huwe1, Herc1, Herc3, Herc4, Herc6, Hecw1, and Hecw2 showed no effect on Ptch1 degradation.
source: We expressed mouse Nedd4 and Nedd4l together with Ptch1-FLAG in HEK293 cells, and found that neither one promoted Ptch1 degradation, and several other HECT-domain E3 ligases including Wwp1, Wwp2, Huwe1, Herc1, Herc3, Herc4, Herc6, Hecw1, and Hecw2 also showed no effect, but co-expression of Smurf1 or Smurf2 did (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5A and represents data from Western blot analysis.

claim: Co-expression of Smurf1 or Smurf2 promoted Ptch1 degradation in HEK293 cells.
source: We expressed mouse Nedd4 and Nedd4l together with Ptch1-FLAG in HEK293 cells, and found that neither one promoted Ptch1 degradation, and several other HECT-domain E3 ligases including Wwp1, Wwp2, Huwe1, Herc1, Herc3, Herc4, Herc6, Hecw1, and Hecw2 also showed no effect, but co-expression of Smurf1 or Smurf2 did (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5A,B and represents data from Western blot analysis.

claim: The ligase deficient Smurf1CA and Smurf2CG mutants failed to influence Ptch1 stability.
source: Consistent with a specific role, the ligase deficient Smurf1CA and Smurf2CG mutants failed to influence Ptch1 stability (Figure 5B).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5B and represents data from Western blot analysis.

claim: Knockdown of either Smurf or both with siRNAs augmented the ciliary localization of Ptch1-GFP in NIH3T3 cells without ShhN treatment.
source: Since the 'PPXY' motif mutants accumulated in cilia, we asked if knockdown of either Smurf or both with siRNAs could augment the ciliary localization of Ptch1-GFP. We found this was the case in NIH3T3 cells without (Figure 5C,D) or with ShhN treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5C,D and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Knockdown of either Smurf or both with siRNAs augmented the ciliary localization of Ptch1-GFP in NIH3T3 cells with ShhN treatment.
source: Since the 'PPXY' motif mutants accumulated in cilia, we asked if knockdown of either Smurf or both with siRNAs could augment the ciliary localization of Ptch1-GFP. We found this was the case in NIH3T3 cells without (Figure 5C,D) or with ShhN treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Smurf2 directs the TGF-β type I receptor and the μ opioid neuropeptide receptor to endocytic turnover.
source: Because Smurf2 is known to direct the TGF-β type I receptor and the μ opioid neuropeptide receptor to endocytic turnover (Di Guglielmo et al., 2003; Henry et al., 2012), we posited that Smurf1 and Smurf2 might be the enzymes that control Ptch1 endocytosis and chose them for further analysis.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Di Guglielmo et al., 2003; Henry et al., 2012).

claim: Individually knockout Smurf1−/− or Smurf2−/− mice are healthy and fertile.
source: Smurf1 and Smurf2 share redundant functions during development as individually knockout Smurf1−/− or Smurf2−/− mice are healthy and fertile, but the embryos lacking both genes were not able to develop to term (Yamashita et al., 2005; Narimatsu et al., 2009; Blank et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Yamashita et al., 2005; Narimatsu et al., 2009; Blank et al., 2012).

claim: Embryos lacking both Smurf1 and Smurf2 genes were not able to develop to term.
source: Smurf1 and Smurf2 share redundant functions during development as individually knockout Smurf1−/− or Smurf2−/− mice are healthy and fertile, but the embryos lacking both genes were not able to develop to term (Yamashita et al., 2005; Narimatsu et al., 2009; Blank et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Yamashita et al., 2005; Narimatsu et al., 2009; Blank et al., 2012).

claim: Silencing Smurf1 and Smurf2 simultaneously in wildtype MEFs completely abolished Shh induction of Gli1.
source: To assess the role of Smurfs in Shh signaling, we quantified the transcriptional responses of endogenous Gli1 by RT-PCR (Figure 5E) and RT-qPCR (Figure 5F) in MEFs with different Smurf genetic background, and found that silencing Smurf1 and Smurf2 simultaneously in wildtype MEFs completely abolished Shh induction of Gli1 (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5E,F and represents data from RT-PCR and RT-qPCR experiments.

claim: MEFs that lack one of the two Smurf genes still mounted a considerable Gli1 transcriptional response to ShhN.
source: MEFs that lack one of the two Smurf genes still mounted a considerable Gli1 transcriptional response to ShhN; however, silencing the remaining Smurf2 allele in Smurf1−/− or Smurf1 allele in Smurf2−/− MEFs, respectively, led to marked curtailment of Gli1 activation (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5E,F and represents data from RT-PCR and RT-qPCR experiments.

claim: Silencing the remaining Smurf2 allele in Smurf1−/− or Smurf1 allele in Smurf2−/− MEFs led to marked curtailment of Gli1 activation.
source: MEFs that lack one of the two Smurf genes still mounted a considerable Gli1 transcriptional response to ShhN; however, silencing the remaining Smurf2 allele in Smurf1−/− or Smurf1 allele in Smurf2−/− MEFs, respectively, led to marked curtailment of Gli1 activation (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5E,F and represents data from RT-PCR and RT-qPCR experiments.

claim: Expression of Smurfs showed a compensatory upregulation in response to the loss of the other Smurf in MEFs.
source: Expression of Smurfs showed a compensatory upregulation in response to the loss of the other Smurf in these MEFs as reported (Yamashita et al., 2005; Tang et al., 2011), but surprisingly, ShhN induced expression of both Smurfs (Figure 5E,G).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5E,G and is supported by citations to previous literature (Yamashita et al., 2005; Tang et al., 2011).

claim: Ad-cre infection-mediated ablation of conditional Smurf2fl alleles in Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs severely dampened the Gli1 transcriptional response to ShhN.
source: In Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs, Ad-cre infection-mediated ablation of conditional Smurf2fl alleles severely dampened the Gli1 transcriptional response to ShhN (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 5H,I and represents data from RT-qPCR and Western blot experiments.

claim: Shh-induced ciliary import of Smo was affected in Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs after Ad-cre infection.
source: Similarly, two other Shh signaling responses, namely Shh-induced ciliary import of Smo and Gli3, were also affected (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 6A-C and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Shh-induced ciliary import of Gli3 was affected in Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs after Ad-cre infection.
source: Similarly, two other Shh signaling responses, namely Shh-induced ciliary import of Smo and Gli3, were also affected (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 6A-C and represents data from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Shh induction of GliBS-luc responses in Ad-cre infected Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs (Smurfs null) can be rescued by reintroducing wildtype Smurf1 or Smurf2 but not mutant Smurf1CA or Smurf2CG cDNA.
source: Since we could rescue Shh induction of GliBS-luc responses in Ad-cre infected Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs (Smurfs null) by reintroducing wildtype Smurf1 or Smurf2 but not mutant Smurf1CA or Smurf2CG cDNA (Figure 6D), or by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Suppressor of fused (Sufu) (Figure 6E), an essential downstream negative regulator of Shh signaling, the observed defects of GliBS-luc induction have to be Smurfs and Shh pathway specific.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 6D and represents data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Shh induction of GliBS-luc responses in Ad-cre infected Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs can be rescued by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Suppressor of fused (Sufu).
source: Since we could rescue Shh induction of GliBS-luc responses in Ad-cre infected Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs (Smurfs null) by reintroducing wildtype Smurf1 or Smurf2 but not mutant Smurf1CA or Smurf2CG cDNA (Figure 6D), or by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Suppressor of fused (Sufu) (Figure 6E), an essential downstream negative regulator of Shh signaling, the observed defects of GliBS-luc induction have to be Smurfs and Shh pathway specific.
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 6E and represents data from luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The observed defects of GliBS-luc induction in Smurf-null cells are Smurfs and Shh pathway specific.
source: Since we could rescue Shh induction of GliBS-luc responses in Ad-cre infected Smurf1−/−;Smurf2fl/fl MEFs (Smurfs null) by reintroducing wildtype Smurf1 or Smurf2 but not mutant Smurf1CA or Smurf2CG cDNA (Figure 6D), or by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Suppressor of fused (Sufu) (Figure 6E), an essential downstream negative regulator of Shh signaling, the observed defects of GliBS-luc induction have to be Smurfs and Shh pathway specific.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue experiments shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Simultaneous inactivation of both Smurf genes and removal of the 'PPXY' motifs of Ptch1 have congruent effects on various Shh signaling events.
source: Taken together, the above results show that simultaneous inactivation of both Smurf genes and removal of the 'PPXY' motifs of Ptch1 have congruent effects on various Shh signaling events, and indicate that a common Smurf function is required at a step upstream from the control of the ciliary import of Smo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data from Figures 3-6 showing similar effects of PPXY deletion and Smurf inactivation.

claim: A common Smurf function is required at a step upstream from the control of the ciliary import of Smo.
source: Taken together, the above results show that simultaneous inactivation of both Smurf genes and removal of the 'PPXY' motifs of Ptch1 have congruent effects on various Shh signaling events, and indicate that a common Smurf function is required at a step upstream from the control of the ciliary import of Smo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing that Smurf inactivation affects Smo ciliary import (Figure 6A-C).

claim: Exogenously expressed Ptch1-RFP colocalized with the ligase deficient, GFP-tagged Smurf2CG mutant in Cav-1 positive lipid rafts at the rim of the plasma membrane in non-permeabilizing MEFs.
source: First, in non-permeabilizing MEFs, we found exogenously expressed Ptch1-RFP colocalized with the ligase deficient, GFP-tagged Smurf2CG mutant in Cav-1 positive lipid rafts at the rim of the plasma membrane (Figure 7A).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7A and represents data from confocal imaging experiments.

claim: Smurfs are preferentially localized in the nucleus.
source: Although first identified as modulators of TGF-β/BMP signaling, Smurfs are preferentially localized in the nucleus (Kavsak et al., 2000) and play a crucial function in maintaining genomic stability (Blank et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Kavsak et al., 2000; Blank et al., 2012).

claim: Smurfs play a crucial function in maintaining genomic stability.
source: Although first identified as modulators of TGF-β/BMP signaling, Smurfs are preferentially localized in the nucleus (Kavsak et al., 2000) and play a crucial function in maintaining genomic stability (Blank et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature (Blank et al., 2012).

claim: Treatment with ShhN ligand caused Smurf2GFP to move from the nucleus to the cytoplasm.
source: Serendipitously, we found that treatment with ShhN ligand or co-expression with Ptch1-RFP each caused Smurf2GFP to move from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and represents data from fluorescence imaging experiments.

claim: Co-expression with Ptch1-RFP caused Smurf2GFP to move from the nucleus to the cytoplasm.
source: Serendipitously, we found that treatment with ShhN ligand or co-expression with Ptch1-RFP each caused Smurf2GFP to move from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and represents data from fluorescence imaging experiments.

claim: Shh signaling could increase the cytoplasmic pool of Smurfs.
source: In light of the Shh induction (Figure 5E,F), these results indicate that Shh signaling could increase the cytoplasmic pool of Smurfs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing Shh-induced Smurf expression (Figure 5E,F) and cytoplasmic redistribution (Figure 7B).

claim: FRET analysis showed that Ptch1-CFP was localized in close proximity with Smurf1-YFP or Smurf2-YFP at punctate intracellular vesicles in MEFs.
source: Third, fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) analysis showed that Ptch1-CFP was localized in close proximity with Smurf1-YFP or Smurf2-YFP at punctate intracellular vesicles in MEFs (Figure 7C,D), and ShhN treatment enhanced this colocalization (Figure 7E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7C,D and represents data from FRET analysis.

claim: ShhN treatment enhanced colocalization of Ptch1-CFP with Smurf1-YFP or Smurf2-YFP.
source: Third, fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) analysis showed that Ptch1-CFP was localized in close proximity with Smurf1-YFP or Smurf2-YFP at punctate intracellular vesicles in MEFs (Figure 7C,D), and ShhN treatment enhanced this colocalization (Figure 7E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7E and represents data from FRET analysis.

claim: Δ2PY-CFP failed to generate FRET with Smurf2-YFP.
source: However, Δ2PY-CFP failed to generate FRET with Smurf2-YFP (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 7C,D and represents data from FRET analysis.

claim: The ligase-deficient Smurf2CG-Myc co-sedimented in the Cav-1-containing 20–25% sucrose fractions readily with Ptch1-FLAG.
source: Theses result were further corroborated in the discontinuous sucrose gradient sedimentation experiment described earlier, in which the ligase-deficient Smurf2CG-Myc co-sedimented in the Cav-1-containing 20–25% sucrose fractions readily with Ptch1-FLAG, whereas Δ2PY was inefficient in bringing Smurf2CG-Myc into these fractions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 1E and represents data from sucrose gradient sedimentation experiments.

claim: Δ2PY was inefficient in bringing Smurf2CG-Myc into Cav-1-containing 20–25% sucrose fractions.
source: Theses result were further corroborated in the discontinuous sucrose gradient sedimentation experiment described earlier, in which the ligase-deficient Smurf2CG-Myc co-sedimented in the Cav-1-containing 20–25% sucrose fractions readily with Ptch1-FLAG, whereas Δ2PY was inefficient in bringing Smurf2CG-Myc into these fractions (Figure 1E).
